@@ -117,7 +117,7 @@ The server exposes tools across three modules in `crates/app/src/mcp/` (see `cra
 - `fit_stock { "shape"?: "box" | "cylinder", "margin"?: number, "sides"?: [number, number, number, number, number, number] }`: Fit the active setup's stock to its parts, never fixtures (including vises, accessories and plates). `shape` defaults to `"box"`; `"cylinder"` fits a Z cylinder snug about the parts. `margin` is the allowance on every side in mm (default 2). `sides` gives six allowances in mm, ordered [-X, +X, -Y, +Y, -Z, +Z], and replaces `margin` (box only). Keeps the stock's rotation. One undo step through `SetStock`; returns `{ stock }`. Refused by name: no models, only fixtures, negative or non-finite allowances, malformed parameters (including a `sides` array without six finite numbers), an unknown shape, `sides` with a cylinder, or models with no usable extent (#1538).
 - `set_raw_stock_only { "on": boolean }`: For a stock made from a model (`set_stock` `from_model`), say whether that source model is raw stock only - a casting or blank you cut into, not the finished part. Default off: the model is judged like every model. On: the gouge verdict leaves it out. One undo step. Refused by name when there is no stock yet ("set the stock first"), when the stock is not made from a model, or when the source model has no geometry. The mark holds only while the model is still the stock's source and its geometry and placement (position and rotation) are unchanged, so moving or turning the model voids it; otherwise it is ignored and the post says so by name. An operation that machines the model (as its source or in a boundary pick) puts it back in the verdict. If the mark leaves nothing to judge, the post is refused by name.
 - `list_tool_catalog {}`: List built-in tool definitions.
-- `add_tool { "catalog"?: string, "definition"?: object, "name"?: string }`: Add a tool: a copy of a `list_tool_catalog` entry, or a full definition (`get_job`'s tool shape); `name` defaults to the catalog name. Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999 that the mounted machine does not reserve (a probe takes the machine's reserved probe pocket; a cutter on a reserved number or name is refused) and returns `number` and `posts_as`. In `add_tool` and `edit_tool` definitions, `cutting_data` rows accept `"material": "unknown"` (the tool's default row, alongside workpiece material words) and optional `stepdown` / `stepover` in mm (`feed` in mm/min); duplicate materials, non-positive or non-finite values, or `stepover` wider than the cutter are refused by name.
+- `add_tool { "catalog"?: string, "definition"?: object, "name"?: string }`: Add a tool: a copy of a `list_tool_catalog` entry, or a full definition (`get_job`'s tool shape); `name` defaults to the catalog name. Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999 that the mounted machine does not reserve (a probe takes the machine's reserved probe pocket; a cutter on a reserved number or name is refused) and returns `number` and `posts_as`. In `add_tool` and `edit_tool` definitions, `cutting_data` rows accept `"material": "unknown"` (the tool's default row, alongside workpiece material words) and optional `stepdown` / `stepover` in mm (`feed` in mm/min); duplicate materials, non-positive or non-finite values, or `stepover` wider than the cutter are refused by name. A form mill (`kind: "form_mill"`, #3369) states `form`: a `preset` (`kind` `roundover`, `cove`, `ogee`, `v_groove` or `bead`, with its numbers) or drawn `points` `[z, r, arc]`, and `pilot_len`. The preset writes the points; the outline sets `diameter` and `flute_len`. Each operation refuses a form mill by name.
 - `edit_tool { "name": string, "patch": object }` (`tool_edit.rs`, #1062): Edit a document tool by its `get_job` `tools[].name`. `patch` is a partial flat `ToolDto`, the shape of `add_tool.definition` and `get_job`'s `tools[].definition`: e.g. `{ "rpm": 4321, "vendor": "Acme" }`. Fields include `kind`, `diameter`, `flute_len`, `rpm`, `feed`, `flutes`, `cutting_data`, `part_number`, `vendor`, `coating`, `helix_deg` and `notes`. JSON merge patch keeps omitted fields and removes optional keys with `null`. Returns `{ tool, definition }` with the updated definition. Runs `ChangeTool` as one undo step; `undo` restores the previous definition and `redo` reapplies it. Operations using changed tool geometry become stale. Refused with a named reason: an unknown or non-tool name, a non-object patch, an unknown field, invalid tool dimensions, catalog values or cutting-data rows, a retype incompatible with an operation, or a change that no longer fits its holder body or drawn cutter. `number`, `body` and `cutter` keys are refused; use `set_tool_number`, the tool-body tools and `set_tool_cutter_profile` for those edits.
 - `delete_tool { "name": string }`: Delete a document tool through the undoable `DeleteTool` (one undo step; undo restores its number, holder body and cutter). Refused by tool name, changing nothing: an unknown name, an entity that is not a tool, or a tool an operation still uses (`set_tool` the operation onto another tool first).
 - `set_tool_number { "tool": string, "number": integer }`: Give a document tool its controller number (the `T..` / `H..` a post writes, matching the machine's tool table). Returns `number` and `posts_as`. One undo step. Refused by name: an unknown or non-tool name, a number outside 1-99999, `null`, a number another tool already has on the same machine, a no-op.

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+## #3369 - a form mill kind with roundover, cove, ogee, V-groove and bead presets
+
+Plan step D2 of the tool library redesign (#3663), stacked on D1 (#3929).
+
+**Decided: the outline lives on `Tool` (`Tool::form`), not only in the
+drawn cutter (`ToolCutter`).** The issue text puts the outline in the
+`ToolDto::cutter` field. But `Tool::meridian`, `Tool::profile` (the band
+stack that the collision checks sweep), `is_sane` and the starter catalog
+see only `Tool`. `ToolCutter` is a document component, and the catalog
+and the tools crate cannot read it. So `Tool` gets one field,
+`form: Option<FormSpec>` (`crates/tools/src/form_mill.rs`): the points
+`[z, r, arc]`, the pilot length and the preset that wrote them. The
+drawn cutter stays what it is for every mill (a drawn neck or shank);
+for a form mill it reads the form through `Tool::profile`, so the two
+agree. Dropped: the outline in `ToolCutter` only (the catalog, the
+meridian and the sanity law could not read it, and a catalog form mill
+would land without its shape).
+
+**Decided: the outline owns the diameter and the flute length.** A form
+mill's `diameter` is twice the outline's widest radius and its
+`flute_len` is the outline's top. `is_sane` refuses a disagreement by
+name and states the right numbers. The editor (`ToolUi::to_tool`) and
+MCP `add_tool` / `edit_tool` call `Tool::settle_form`, which writes the
+points from the preset and the two numbers from the points. The editor
+shows the two numbers and does not take them. A file load does not
+settle: a file that disagrees is refused, not repaired. Dropped: a
+separate stated diameter (two sources for one number).
+
+**Decided: with a preset, the stored points are exactly what the preset
+writes.** The file keeps both the preset and the points, so a reader
+needs no preset code to draw the form, and `is_sane` refuses points that
+disagree with their preset. A catalog entry states only the preset; the
+reader fills the points (`form_mill::fill`) and keeps the stated
+diameter, so `is_sane` checks the catalog numbers. A preset can be
+dropped (`preset: null`) to keep a drawn outline.
+
+**Decided: no file version step.** Only the `form_mill` kind states a
+`form`, and each older build (D1's included) refuses the unknown kind
+word by name. It cannot read a form mill as another tool. The
+`.camproj` stays at its version and the `.camtools` library does not
+step (a test pins that it stays under `TIP_FORM_VERSION`). Dropped: a
+`.camtools` version 7 and a `.camproj` version 80 (no reader needs them).
+
+**Decided: the presets and their numbers.** Our own geometry from the
+terms of the public router bit catalogues: roundover (concave quarter
+arc), cove (convex quarter arc), ogee (concave arc, flat step, convex
+arc), V-groove (cone with an optional tangent tip ball, no pilot), bead
+(a flat step, the quirk, then a concave quarter arc). Each preset with a
+pilot starts its cut at the pilot radius. The pilot segments (the tip
+face and the bearing side, up to `pilot_len`) are flagged non-cutting in
+the meridian. Dropped: a pilot radius apart from the cutter's start
+radius (no catalogue bit that this slice covers needs it).
+
+**Decided: no undercut in this slice.** The radius must not narrow
+upward: a line that narrows, a convex arc past its widest point or a
+concave arc before its narrowest point is refused by name with #896.
+
+**Decided: every operation refuses a form mill by name.** The form mill
+is in the `CONE` family (2D Chamfer, Deburr and the multi-axis cone
+kinds), so `no_orphan_tool_kinds` holds. `tool_gate` refuses it at the
+creation door and at the generation and post door, and the 2D Chamfer
+refusal names the edge form work (#896). No refusal suggests a form mill
+(`kinds_phrase` drops it beside a kind that cuts), and no operation
+offers one. The operation stamp hashes the whole outline and the pilot.
+
+**Decided: the editor.** The kind is in the type list; a "Form preset"
+list (a drawn outline or one of the five presets), the preset's number
+rows and the pilot length show on the Tool tab (`tool_form_mill_row.rs`,
+called from `kind_rows()`). A drawn outline is edited through MCP
+`edit_tool`; the editor shows it and does not draw point by point. The
+shape window's Draw cutter view names the form in place of a tip number.
+Dropped: a point table for the form in the editor (later work, with
